ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on the Regulation of Specified Financial Transaction Information and the Financial Transaction Reports Act, as amended by Korea's AML/CFT reform, along with Articles 288 through 317 of the Korean Commercial Act for Chusik Hoesa formation; Presidential Decree and Financial Services Commission / Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) CDD and beneficial owner rules.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (certified extract from the corporate registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court of Korea Registry Office with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route (if receiving state is an Apostille Convention member): Korean notary public certification if required, then Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) Apostille. Consular Legalization route (if receiving state is not a member): Korean notary public certification, then MOFA authentication, then legalization by the destination-state embassy or consulate in Seoul. The two routes are parallel, mutually exclusive alternatives and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (tax compliance and active corporate status certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service (with active-status reference from the Supreme Court Registry Office)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille: notarization -> MOFA Apostille. Consular Legalization: notarization -> MOFA authentication -> destination consular legalization in Seoul. Each document uses only one of these two paths depending on the destination state's membership in the Apostille Convention.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney for pre-incorporation representation and bank/authority filing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Chusik Hoesa, notarized by a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Apostille states: notary certification -> MOFA Apostille. For non-Apostille states: notary certification -> MOFA authentication -> destination consular legalization. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive and are never used in combination on the same instrument.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founders of the Chusik Hoesa, deposited and registered with the Supreme Court Registry Office and notarized as required
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille: certified copy -> notarization (if private signature) -> MOFA Apostille. Consular Legalization: certified copy -> notarization -> MOFA authentication -> destination embassy/consulate legalization. Select only the path required by the destination jurisdiction.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean commercial bank maintaining the entity's deposit and trade finance relationship
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille Convention state: bank officer's signature notarized -> MOFA Apostille. Non-member state: bank officer's signature notarized -> MOFA authentication -> destination consular legalization. The two paths are exclusive; sequential chaining is prohibited.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening before onboarding each shareholder, director, officer, ultimate beneficial owner (UBO), signatory, material counterparty, freight forwarder, rail operator, consignor and consignee against the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) guidance, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, United Nations Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, EU consolidated lists where applicable, Korean national sanctions and financial sanctions notices, FATF public statements, and domestic adverse media. Every dossier must contain exact name transliterations and homophones, date and place of birth, passport or Korean resident registration number only where lawful, nationality, address, corporate group tree, politically exposed person (PEP) status, family and close-associate links, and false-positive resolution. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for foreign and domestic PEPs, and screening must be refreshed continuously, at each registry event and before every SWIFT wire or letter of credit payment.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Service (Court Registry Office corporate name search and reservation portal)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be registered in Korean Hangul as the primary local script. A foreign-language trade name is permitted only through faithful phonetic transliteration into Hangul and, if used in English, as a supplementary registered name. The four-tier naming convention requires: (1) the mandatory corporate-form token 'Chusik Hoesa'; (2) a distinctive Hangul word that is not homophonically similar to an existing registered company in the same business category; (3) optional descriptive business-purpose words, e.g., rail logistics, freight agency or international transport; and (4) if desired, a short-form English name or transliterated mark. The registry compares Hangul consonants, vowels, spacing and phonetic variants before

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), in particular Articles 167, 289, 295 through 317 and 330; Foreign Investment Promotion Act; Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; Notary Public Act; Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporate Registration Division, Seoul Central District Court Registry Office, Court Administration of the Supreme Court of Korea
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Incorporation Registration Application and Certified Articles of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for a Chusik Hoesa under the Commercial Act. However, before the incorporation registration, the full issue price of all subscribed shares must be paid into a blocked escrow subscription account at a licensed commercial bank in Korea. The deposit is blocked and may not be withdrawn until the certificate of incorporation registration is issued. A practical benchmark of at least KRW 100,000,000 is required by most logistics licensing authorities to demonstrate capital adequacy for international freight forwarding. Foreign investors must deposit through a foreign exchange bank and file a foreign investment report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, with the same escrow restriction preserved until registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF CHUSIK HOESA (STOCK CORPORATION) FOR INCORPORATION AND CORPORATE GOVERNANCE. RESOLUTION NUMBER 2025-FBD-001, ADOPTED BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT OF ALL DIRECTORS. The undersigned, being the entirety of the Board of Directors of the corporation to be formed as a Chusik Hoesa under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, having reviewed the promoters report and all attached documents, hereby waive any formal meeting requirements and resolve as follows. First, the Board ratifies and adopts the Articles of Incorporation executed by the incorporators, including the corporate purpose of transcontinental container block train intermodal expedited freight forwarding under ISIC 5229, the authorized share capital, the classes of shares, and the registered office clause. The Board accepts the subscriptions to shares as listed in the promoters share subscription ledger and directs the Representative Director to ensure payment of the full issue amount of each subscribed share before registration. All capital payments shall be made to a blocked escrow subscription account at a licensed commercial bank, and no withdrawal shall be permitted until the company has been entered in the commercial registry and the certificate of incorporation registration has been issued. Second, the Board adopts the registered office set forth in the Articles of Incorporation as the companys principal executive seat and authorized administrative domicile. The corporate secretary or statutory agent is directed to execute the lease, to file the registered office address in the commercial registry, and to maintain the address in all corporate books and public filings. Third, the Board authorizes the establishment of one or more operating bank accounts at a licensed bank in the Republic of Korea. The Representative Director and the Chief Financial Officer shall be joint signatories, and the Board specifically authorizes SWIFT wire transfers, export and import letters of credit, documentary collections, foreign exchange purchases and settlements, and the opening of any related trade finance facility necessary for the transcontinental rail freight forwarding business. Fourth, the Board appoints the following statutory officers: the Representative Director, the Chief Financial Officer, one external auditor, and a non-statutory corporate secretary. Each appointee has accepted the appointment in writing and shall execute declarations of acceptance to be filed with the registration court. The external auditor shall perform the independent monitoring duties imposed by the Commercial Act and shall not serve in any executive capacity. Fifth, the Board delegates to the Representative Director the authority to submit the incorporation registration application, to apply for tax and value added tax registration, to procure all ministerial and municipal operating licenses, to instruct legal counsel for international freight forwarding and rail logistics registrations, and to take any further measure that is necessary or convenient to render the corporation operational in full compliance with Korean law. The Board acknowledges that legal personality commences only upon registration. This resolution shall be effective as of incorporation and may be certified as a unanimous written resolution in lieu of a meeting, with full force and effect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Notarisation of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Name Reservation Window, Seoul Central District Court Registry Office, and a Notary Public licensed under the Notary Public Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Reserve the corporate name online in the court registry name reservation system, confirming that the name ends with Chusik Hoesa and is not identical to any pre-existing registered entity. Prepare an official Korean-language draft of the Articles of Incorporation containing the corporate purpose, authorized shares, par value, registered office address, number and powers of directors, and public notice method. Each promoter must sign the draft in the presence of the notary; if a promoter is abroad, execute a power of attorney for a Korean representative, legalise or apostille the signature, and submit it to the notary. The notary verifies legal capacity and statutory content, certifies the execution date, and issues a notarial certificate and certified copies. Any defect in mandatory articles must be cured before proceeding.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation in Korean language
Passport or foreign registration card of each promoter
Corporate name reservation certificate
Power of attorney and notarised or apostilled signature sheet if promoter is abroad
Registered office lease agreement or owner consent form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry refuses the name reservation, select a new proposed name and reserve again; if the notary requires additional legalisation, obtain the missing consular or apostille certification and re-attend the notary. The process is curable by re-submission, and there is no adverse long-term record once corrected.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Subscription and Blocked Escrow Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorised commercial bank under the Banking Act and foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, with Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency notification for foreign investors
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a dedicated escrow subscription account in the name of the company in formation. Each promoter and subscriber shall pay the full issue price of the subscribed shares in Korean won into that account. The bank shall issue a deposit receipt and a balance certificate naming the account number, the depositor, the total amount, and the blocked nature of the funds. No withdrawal may occur before the completion of incorporation registration; the bank will request the incorporated company registration certificate for release of funds. For a foreign investor, file the foreign investment report with the foreign exchange bank or KOTRA under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, and preserve the foreign exchange transaction receipt as evidence of lawful capital import.
required_dossiers: Subscription ledger in the name of the company
Passport or business identification of each promoter
Foreign investment report where applicable
Source of funds evidence such as bank statements or remittance confirmation
Bank account application form and escrow agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank questions the source of funds, provide certified bank statements, an explanation letter, and the underlying commercial contract or inheritance documents. If the balance certificate is incomplete, request the bank to reissue it in the exact corporate formation name; a defect is cured by the bank amendment without invalidating the subscription.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Registration at the District Court Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Registrar, Seoul Central District Court Registry Office, under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the notarised Articles of Incorporation and capital deposit certificate are available, submit the incorporation registration application to the court registry. The application must state the corporate name, the registered office, the amount of paid-in capital, the number of shares issued, the par value, the names and resident information of the directors and auditor, and the method of public notice. The registrar will review the statutory conditions of the Commercial Act and the legal viability of the corporate purpose. When satisfied, the registry enters the company in the commercial register and issues the incorporation registration certificate. Legal personality commences on that registration date. The original notarised documents must be preserved in the registry file.
required_dossiers: Completed incorporation registration application form
Certified true copy of the notarised Articles of Incorporation
Capital deposit certificate and bank balance certificate
List of shares subscribed and payment record
Written acceptance declarations from each director and the auditor
Registered office lease and written owner consent
Court registration fee payment receipt
Power of attorney if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a correction order, file the requested supplemental materials within two weeks. If the application is rejected, either file an immediate appeal to the appellate court under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act or, after curing the legal defect, resubmit a new application with a new fee. Correction responses are not treated as default judgements and the corporate formation remains valid after proper cure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Tax and Business Registration with the National Tax Service and Local Municipality
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service district tax office having jurisdiction over the registered office, together with the local Si-Gun-Gu municipal business licensing office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month after incorporation, file the corporate incorporation report with the district tax office and obtain the corporate taxpayer identification number and the business registration certificate. Complete the corporate tax registration dossier, register for value added tax and electronic tax invoice issuance, and formally notify the municipality of the place of business. The business scope in the tax register must correspond to ISIC 5229 and to the commercial model of transcontinental container block train intermodal expedited freight forwarding. If the company is foreign owned, register the representative director as the taxpayer contact and file any required foreign investment reporting. Retain the tax registration certificate for opening permanent operating bank accounts and for applying to the licensing authorities.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation registration
Certified copy of the Articles of Incorporation
Passport or national identity card of the representative director
Registered office lease and land registry extract
Corporate seal registration certificate
Business registration application form for value added tax
Foreign exchange bank certificate if foreign owned
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office requests proof of the place of business, provide a certified copy of the lease, utility bill in the corporate name, and an on-site photograph. Late filing is cured by paying the minimal non-filing surcharge and submitting the overdue report through the HomeTax system. The National Tax Service does not cancel the entity for a cureble delay of the initial registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: International Freight Forwarding and Rail Intermodal Operating Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, Railway and Logistics Policy Division; Korea International Freight Forwarders Association; and local municipal government if a container yard or logistics facility is operated
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the operating registration dossier for the international freight forwarding and rail intermodal expediting business. The authority will examine the paid-in capital, the professional qualifications of the logistics management staff, the registered office, and the existence of block train slot contracts with railway operators. If the company owns or operates a container transloading facility, a container yard, or a logistics terminal, apply separately to the local government for the logistics facility permit and to the railway infrastructure authority for any track-side interface approval. Demonstrate cargo liability insurance and a communication system capable of real-time rail shipment tracking. The operating registration certificate must be displayed at the principal office.
required_dossiers: Completed forwarder registration application form
Business registration certificate
Articles of incorporation and corporate seal certificate
Proof of paid-in capital and capital deposit certificate
Contracts or confirmed booking agreements with railway or block train operators
Cargo liability insurance policy certificate
Logistics facility site plan and floor plan where applicable
Evidence of professional qualifications of logistics personnel
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the regulator queries the rail operator agreements, submit interim booking orders or letters of capacity from the block train operator pending final contract execution. If a site inspection identifies insufficient safety equipment, complete the required upgrades and request a reinspection. Operating activities cannot commence before the registration certificate is issued, but the application may be supplemented without prejudice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Fire Safety, Occupational Health, and Environmental Clearance for Physical Intermodal Operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Fire Agency; Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency; local municipal fire and environmental authorities; Korea Railroad Safety Authority for siding interface matters
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain fire safety completion inspection and civil defense fire clearance for the registered office, container transloading area, or warehouse. Submit the building plan, fire fighting system design documents, evacuation arrangements, and proof of installation of fire extinguishing equipment. File an occupational safety and health plan with the Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency and prepare chemical inventory documentation for diesel powered equipment such as forklifts and terminal tractors. For a site of at least 1,000 square meters but less than 5,000 square meters, file the small-scale environmental impact review with the local environmental agency. Secure wastewater discharge registration if wheel-washing or drainage facilities exist, and retained hazardous waste disposal contracts with licensed handlers.
required_dossiers: Fire fighting system installation completion certificate
Structural safety declaration for the building or open yard
Fire protection inspection application form
Occupational safety and health management plan
Material safety data sheets for fuel and chemicals
Wastewater discharge or storm water management registration
Hazardous waste disposal service contract
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For a fire safety rejection, correct the listed deficiencies, obtain the contractors certificate, and apply for reinspection. If the environmental agency requires additional impact assessment, submit the requested abatement study and implement the proposed mitigation measures. Each certificate is independent, and the company may operate office-based forwarding activity while facility remediation is completed, provided no physical transloading begins before the final clearance is issued.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, Railway and Logistics Policy Division; Korea International Freight Forwarders Association; local municipal government business licensing division; National Fire Agency; Ministry of Environment and local Gu-Si-Gun environmental review office
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: International Freight Forwarding Agency Registration with intermodal rail cargo endorsement, together with a Logistics Facility Permit and Civil Defense Fire Safety Certificate if the entity operates a container yard, transloading station, or warehouse

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea and the local Gu-Si-Gun environmental review office
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Small-scale Environmental Impact Review (Pre-environmental Review) for goods loading and unloading or container storage areas from 1,000 square meters to 5,000 square meters; full Environmental Impact Assessment Report is not required for office-based transcontinental forwarding activity or for existing industrial logistics buildings below the threshold
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharged to public sewer from wheel-washing or stormwater collection systems must meet BOD concentration not exceeding 10 mg/L and suspended solids not exceeding 20 mg/L. Diesel powered non-road cargo handling equipment must comply with the Clean Air Conservation Act PM emission limit not exceeding 0.015 g/kWh after 2025, and VOC emissions from any fuel storage or container transloading area must remain below a total hydrocarbon concentration of 50 mg/m3 at the facility boundary. Hazardous waste including used engine oil, hydraulic fluid, and diesel filters must be stored in sealed watertight containers and disposed of exclusively through a licensed waste handler.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain a building fire safety completion inspection certificate from the National Fire Agency system, a civil defense fire safety certificate for the operational site, and an occupational safety and health clearance from the Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency. If diesel fuel storage exceeds 1,000 liters, obtain a dangerous goods storage permit. Provide structural load approval for any rail siding, crane, or container handling equipment, and secure a railway-interface access approval from the Korea Railroad Safety Authority before operations adjacent to any operational rail corridor.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of South Korea; electronic portal HomeTax (hometax.go.kr); Korea Customs Service (KCS) for export clearance via UNI-PASS.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Determine the taxable place of business in Korea (or absence thereof) and whether the entity is a domestic Chusik Hoesa or a non-resident foreign corporation. Step 2: File a business registration application (TIN/VAT registration) with the District Tax Office having jurisdiction over the Korean place of business through HomeTax or in person. Step 3: Submit statutory corporate documents, including articles of incorporation, foreign corporate registration evidence, a Korean place-of-business lease or branch establishment record, board resolution or power of attorney appointing a local tax representative, and any Foreign Investment Promotion Act registration for foreign investment. Step 4: NTS issues a 10-digit Business Registration Number (TIN/VAT ID) and Business Registration Certificate. Step 5: Register as a VAT taxpayer and e-Tax invoice issuer; obtain HomeTax credentials and, if handling exports, a UNI-PASS user ID from Korea Customs Service. Step 6: For a non-resident foreign entity without a fixed domestic place of business, appoint a Korean tax representative and complete HomeTax simplified foreign entity registration to obtain a temporary business registration number before supplying taxable services in Korea.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korean tax law does not provide a check-the-box pass-through election for a Chusik Hoesa; the stock corporation is taxed as an entity under the Corporate Tax Act. No separate hybrid mismatch entity classification election is available to foreign or domestic shareholders; anti-hybrid rules operate under the OECD BEPS framework and Korean tax treaties.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: KRW 0 for a corporate VAT taxpayer; a Chusik Hoesa engaged in rail freight forwarding must register before commencing supplies. The KRW 80,000,000 simplified taxpayer turnover cap is limited to eligible individual micro-businesses and does not apply to a corporation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: A corporate freight forwarder must issue an electronic tax invoice (e-Tax Invoice) through the NTS HomeTax system for taxable B2B supplies. The e-Tax invoice data is transmitted to the NTS at issuance through the HomeTax portal or approved API; NTS validates the recipient business registration number and matches invoice data for VAT return compliance. Korean VAT does not use a national anti-fraud digital stamp or preclearance stamp; enforcement is through HomeTax e-invoice collection matching, penalty surcharges for late/non-filing, and KCS export clearance data matching.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Article 21 of the Value-Added Tax Act zero-rates exported goods and qualifying exported services. A Korean Chusik Hoesa can claim 0% VAT on international rail freight forwarding when the services are supplied for the export of goods from Korea or for the transportation of goods between foreign countries, and when the service is arranged for and paid by a non-resident in foreign currency. The freight forwarder must retain KCS export declarations, transport contracts, railway bills and foreign exchange receipt evidence proving the goods crossed Korea Customs and the consideration was received from outside Korea.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service Export Declaration (UNI-PASS export clearance record, not a Bill of Entry)
Bill of Lading or multimodal rail waybill covering the Eurasian block train or onward sea leg
Commercial invoice and packing list for the exported goods
Foreign Exchange Receipt / Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank
Electronic tax invoice marked zero-rated for the export freight forwarding supply
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS and Korea Customs Service will cross-check the export declaration number, bill of lading, container/railcar identifiers, and the foreign currency receipt. If zero-rating is unsupported or the export documents are false, the supply is reclassified as taxable domestic VAT at 10%. NTS will assess the unpaid VAT with statutory surcharges for false or insufficient VAT returns, monthly late payment interest, and may claw back any VAT refund already paid. Fraudulent zero-rating invoices or forged customs documents also trigger criminal penalties under the Value-Added Tax Act and Korea Customs Act, and an extended statutory tax audit period applies in cases of deliberate concealment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) as the central monetary authority, operating alongside the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as the principal foreign exchange policy authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA), with delegated implementation exercised by foreign exchange banks and reporting through the Korea Financial Telecommunications & Clearings Institute (KFTC)/Foreign Exchange Information Network (FEIN)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a fundamentally open current account and a regulated but operationally efficient capital account. The Korean won is freely convertible for current-account trade in goods and services, including rail freight revenue, logistics service fees, Intermodal transport charges, agency commissions, and ordinary corporate operating expenses under FETA. A resident Chusik Hoesa may receive freight and logistics settlement proceeds in foreign currency and may maintain foreign currency accounts at authorized domestic foreign exchange banks without requiring a pre-approval license for standard operational transactions. Capital account transactions, including inbound equity investment, foreign borrowing, cross-border guarantees, and certain advances, require advance declaration, registration, or follow-up reporting through a specified foreign exchange bank or the BOK/MOEF system. The Korean regulatory framework does not impose mandatory surrender of export freight proceeds into KRW; instead, the duty is to collect, settle, and report proceeds through a domestic foreign exchange bank within prescribed timelines. Freight receivables, unpaid supplier invoices, and profit remittances to non-resident shareholders must be supported by underlying signed contracts, invoices, customs or railway consignment documentation, audited financial statements, and evidence of FDI registration where applicable. Inbound equity capital subscribed by foreign investors is subject to the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and requires advance notification to an authorized bank, opening of a foreign-investment capital account, and issuance of a foreign investment report certificate before capital verification and profit repatriation become compliant. Dividend remittance is not barred or subject to arbitrary approval under routine conditions, but a domestic withholding tax event arises simultaneously with the remittance and requires an accurate Corporate Tax and Withholding Tax filing under Korean tax law. In crisis conditions, FETA empowers BOK and MOEF to impose temporary control measures, but for ordinary rail freight and freight-forwarding treasury operations, no material convertibility hurdle exists.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under FETA and its Enforcement Decree, a resident exporter or cross-border service provider is required to receive export proceeds through an authorized foreign exchange bank within the payment term stated in the underlying contract, generally no later than 4 months from the export declaration date if no specific credit term is documented. The bank must be notified of the collection with the relevant trade/service declaration reference. There is no mandatory conversion ratio requiring surrender of foreign currency to KRW; the mandatory ratio is effectively 0% of export proceeds. The proceeds may lawfully be credited to a domestic foreign currency account or used for permitted current-account settlement, but every receipt must be reportable to BOK/MOEF through FEIN and traceable to the rail freight or logistics service contract, CIM/SMGS consignment note, waybill, or equivalent transport document. Failure to collect within the statutory timeline requires a formal extension application before the deadline, supported by evidence of the buyer default, insurance claim, or amended payment terms.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign-Investment Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational KRW/FCY Current Account
Foreign-Investment Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational KRW/FCY Current Account
Foreign-Investment Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational KRW/FCY Current Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore digital EMI providers are not legal substitutes for a Tier-1 domestic bank account in South Korea. An EMI that is not licensed under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act cannot independently serve as the principal settlement bank for a Korean resident Chusik Hoesa, hold KRW IBANs, or clear trade proceeds through the Korean interbank system. Cross-border fintech platforms operating through a Korean bank partner may be used only as auxiliary collection and FX execution channels, and the account structure must ultimately settle through a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank. For a rail freight and intermodal forwarding entity, the compliance viability of an offshore EMI is low due to FEIN reporting obligations, trade declaration matching, and the need for local bank issuance of Letters of Credit and documentary guarantees.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is required at account opening. At least one representative director, or an appointed director with formal corporate power of attorney and appropriate local registration evidence, must appear at a domestic branch for a face-to-face customer due diligence interview. Foreign directors residing outside Korea may satisfy the initial interview through an apostilled and notarized power of attorney combined with a live remote video interview, but major banks nevertheless require an in-branch visit by the foreign shareholder/UBO or by a resident Korean director with statutory signatory authority before fully activating foreign-currency payment and trade settlement functionalities. Pure consular or remote-only proxy opening without any physical visit is generally not accepted by Tier-1 Korean commercial banks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign UBO with unclear source of equity funds and no local financial footprint in Korea
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled/certified copy of UBO passport, certified corporate registry extract of the parent or individual shareholder, notarized share register, six to twelve months of personal/corporate bank statements evidencing source of funds, certified source-of-wealth statement, tax residence confirmation, and an independent profile of the UBO covering identity, business background, and any prior bankruptcy or regulatory action.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border rail freight forwarder with fast-moving third-party disbursements to multiple jurisdictions, creating potential mismatch between shipping documents and financial flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed rail freight contracts, CIM/SMGS consignment notes, railway waybills, terminal handling receipts, customs declarations, FEIN trade declaration receipts, supplier invoices, container handover documents, insurance certificates, and a complete reconciliation workbook mapping each payment instruction to an underlying physical or multi-modal transport shipment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or PEP risk arising from freight corridor counterparties, consolidators, or end-customers domiciled in higher-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening report with positive hit explanations, independent background investigation on all shareholders and material counterparties, PEP self-declaration, source-of-wealth disclosure, copies of trade certifications and export/import licenses, and a written compliance undertaking confirming the entity has no business with specially designated nationals, embargoed territories, or diverted dual-use cargo.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directorship and negative-magnetic-centre risk where the Korean Chusik Hoesa lacks substantive operational substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease agreement and utility invoices for the Korean registered office, local employee payroll records or outsourcing agreements, corporate seal registration, board resolutions appointing local operating and financial authority, statutory books, tax registration certificate, and a confirmation letter from a licensed Korean certified public accountant regarding planned Korean operational substance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital contributions from non-resident shareholders must be structured as Foreign Direct Investment under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. Before remittance, the investor or domestic entity must file an advance investment report through an authorized foreign exchange bank or Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA). The bank opens a foreign-investment capital account, and the remitter sends the equity contribution by SWIFT MT103 with the designated FDI purpose code and a clear remittance narrative citing the issued foreign investment report number. Upon receipt and verification of the foreign exchange bank memorandum, the entity obtains the foreign investment report certificate and completes capital verification through the bank memorandum. Inbound freight contract receivables are treated as current-account service receipts and may be received through a domestic foreign currency account using the transport service purpose code; the proceeds must be matched against the export of services declaration filed with the relevant customs authority and FEIN.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: All outbound treasury disbursements are settled through the domestic foreign exchange settlement system using SWIFT MT103 for freight payments, Intermodal operator fees, terminal handling charges, insurance and general operational expenses. For larger structured settlements, trade-related disbursements should be executed through irrevocable documentary Letters of Credit or documentary collections where the payee requires proof of payment against consignment note, CIM/SMGS waybill, customs pack, and commercial invoice. Every foreign-currency disbursement must be tagged with the correct FETA transaction purpose code, supported by the underlying service or goods contract, and reported through FEIN so that settlement records reconcile with Korean customs import/export declarations and tax invoices. The bank may require prior receipt of the export proceeds certificate for service income in order to approve outward remittance of dividends or shareholder loans, and dividend remittance must additionally be supported by audited retained earnings, tax withholding confirmation, and resolution of the shareholders meeting.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore forward foreign exchange contracts (KRW/USD, KRW/EUR, KRW/CNY) permitted only where there is genuine current-account or capital-account underlying exposure derived from rail freight revenue, transport receivables, or trade payables, with the trade-related documentary evidence submitted to the foreign exchange bank

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) available principally to non-resident counterparties or in approved offshore hedging structures; Korean resident entities may access onshore NDF equivalents only when the hedging requirement strictly mirrors approved cross-border transaction exposure and satisfies FETA underlying-transaction documentation rules

Cross-currency swaps permitted for the reduction of balance-sheet currency and interest-rate mismatch on documented trade finance or FDI-related borrowings, subject to bank approval, FEIN reporting, and absence of speculative intent
Standard FX options and structured collars may be offered by Korean banks only when embedded within a genuine hedging framework and approved by the bank’s foreign exchange compliance committee

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary General Shareholders Meeting with approval of annual financial statements, election or re-appointment of directors and auditors, and confirmation of statutory registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders in the ordinary general meeting; minutes of the meeting and supporting financial statements must be retained at the registered office and, if statutory audit applies, attached to the corporate income tax return filed with the National Tax Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the fiscal year end; for a December 31 fiscal year end, by March 31, with a two-week advance notice period to shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors may be subject to administrative fines under the Korean Commercial Act, shareholders may petition the court for permission to convene the meeting, and an audit qualification may cause the National Tax Service to refuse the certified financial statements as a valid tax return attachment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return including tax adjustment statement, audited financial statements where subject to external audit, and supporting schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of South Korea through the HomeTax electronic system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 for a December 31 fiscal year end; automatically extended to April 30 when the return is prepared and signed by a qualified tax accountant or certified public accountant under the Corporate Tax Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing negligence surcharge of 20 percent of the unpaid tax, false or unfaithful return surcharge of up to 40 percent of the underpaid tax, late payment surcharge of 0.022 percent per day on the delinquent amount, enforced asset seizure, and repeated non-filing with no business activity for five years may trigger administrative closure and court dissolution with cancellation of commercial registration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local income tax surtax on ordinary corporate tax payable to the local government where the registered head office is located
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government tax office at the registered head office address through WETAX or the local tax electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: April 30 for a December 31 fiscal year end when the corporate tax return is filed by March 31; if the corporate tax return is extended to April 30, the local income tax surtax is due by May 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing and unfaithful return surcharges apply in parallel with national corporate tax surcharges, late payment interest accrues at 0.022 percent per day, and the local government may proceed with compulsory collection against bank accounts and other assets

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Interim corporate tax prepayment for the first half of the fiscal year, together with the related local income tax surtax installment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service for the corporate interim prepayment; local government tax office for the local surtax installment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: August 31 for a December 31 fiscal year end; the local income tax surtax installment is due by September 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Underpayment and non-payment expose the company to the same 0.022 percent per day late payment surcharge and a negligence surcharge of up to 20 percent of the deficient interim tax amount

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External audit report filing for companies meeting the statutory audit threshold, including disclosure of the independent auditor opinion
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service through the DART electronic disclosure system and concurrent attachment to the National Tax Service corporate income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The audit report must be completed and presented to shareholders before the ordinary general meeting and must be filed with the National Tax Service by the corporate income tax return due date, normally March 31 or extended April 30 for a December 31 fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to commission the statutory audit or file the audit report may result in administrative negligence fines up to the amounts prescribed under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, rejection of the un-audited financial statements as a valid corporate tax return attachment, designation of an auditor by the Financial Supervisory Service, and referral for criminal sanctions in cases of fraud

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual maintenance and audit of the shareholder register, director register, charges register, and corporate minute book, including beneficial ownership verification for banking and foreign investment purposes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company secretary, board of directors, and registered office; no separate annual governmental UBO filing is required for a private Chusik Hoesa absent a reportable foreign investment event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually before the ordinary general meeting, and promptly upon any share transfer or change in directors, auditors, or registered charges; Korea does not impose a 30-day commercial register filing window for ordinary private share transfers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors may be liable for damages caused by defective or untimely register updates, the company may face administrative fines under the Commercial Act, and unregistered transferees cannot exercise shareholder rights against the company

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Preservation and availability of statutory corporate books, accounting records, audit documents, and register evidence for inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered office of the Chusik Hoesa and, on demand, the National Tax Service and relevant authorities; required as an internal corporate governance obligation rather than a paid filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be maintained continuously for the statutory retention period, and the annual recorded review must be completed before the corporate tax return is submitted
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Destruction, concealment, or failure to preserve statutory records can result in administrative fines, adverse tax documentation claims, inability to substantiate deductions, and director liability

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Chusik Hoesa is legally required to undergo an independent certified public accountant audit under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies if its total assets at the end of the fiscal year are at least KRW 12 billion approximately USD 9 million; if it is a listed company or is required to submit a business report under the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act; if it is designated as a public-interest company by the Financial Services Commission; if it is consolidated by an audit-subject parent requiring audited subsidiary accounts; or if a competent court or agency orders an audit. Balance sheet size is the principal objective threshold; turnover and headcount do not independently trigger statutory audit for a private Chusik Hoesa, but the Financial Services Commission may designate a company based on public interest criteria, and any company required by another applicable statute to prepare certified financial statements must comply.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements of audit-subject companies must be prepared in accordance with Korean International Financial Reporting Standards where the company is listed or classified as a public-interest entity; non-listed private Chusik Hoesa companies subject to external audit may apply the Korea Non-Public Entity Accounting Standards which are the generally accepted Korean GAAP for non-public companies. Tax returns must be filed in Korean Won and in

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national Corporate Income Tax on the top bracket (taxable income above KRW 300 billion) plus a 10% local income tax surtax, producing a combined top effective headline rate of 26.4%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Foreign-invested enterprises in designated Free Economic Zones and Foreign Investment Zones may enjoy a 100% corporate income tax holiday for the first 5 years and a 50% reduction for the following 2 years under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and Restriction of Special Taxation Act; special credits are available for R&D expenditure, facility investment, job creation, increase in investment, and technology transfer income; no standalone patent box applies, but qualifying technology transfer and qualifying patent royalties may benefit from reduced taxation or tax credits

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Final Return (Settlement of Tax Base and Tax Amount) together with Local Income Tax Return; electronic filing through the National Tax Service HomeTax (hometax.go.kr) system, including the Report of International Transactions and associated financial statements
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; interim corporate income tax prepayments are required semi-annually, but the final statutory return is filed once per fiscal year
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Under Article 60 of the Corporate Income Tax Act, the final return must be filed within three months from the end of the fiscal year, i.e. by March 31 for a calendar-year Chusik Hoesa; an extension of up to one month may be available on application where foreign accounts or non-resident ownership require additional time

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Taxpayer Identification and Corporate Registry Data
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, 10-digit business registration number, representative director, head office address, ISIC code, fiscal year, and shareholding schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact Korean legal name of the Chusik Hoesa and the business registration number. In the shareholder schedule, declare every non-resident corporate and individual shareholder by foreign jurisdiction, tax identification number, ownership percentage, and any chain of intermediate holding companies. Non-resident directors and ultimate beneficial owners must be identified; if the place of effective management is outside Korea, the entity may be reclassified for tax purposes, so the registered office and board decision records must be retained

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Gross Revenue and Sales Reconciliation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report total gross revenue from transcontinental container block train expedited freight forwarding, intermodal haulage, rail tariff rebilling, terminal handling, demurrage charges, storage fees, and ancillary logistics commissions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Korean-resident Chusik Hoesa is taxed on worldwide income, so all foreign revenue from the Eurasia rail corridor must be included. If this entity is a Korean permanent establishment of a non-resident rail freight operator, only Korean-source income attributable to the Korean PE is reported. Revenue routed through a Hong Kong, Singapore, or other non-resident booking company with no substance must be supported by rail bills of lading, CIM/SMGS consignment notes, and intercompany service agreements; otherwise NTS may recharacterise the booking company as a conduit

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Tax Adjustments from Accounting Profit to Taxable Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Set out non-deductible expenses, temporary differences, and permanent differences including entertainment expense limits, depreciation differences, provisions, donations, fines, and excessive intercompany charges
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back all payments to non-resident affiliated entities that fail the arm's-length standard, including freight forwarding commissions, wagon lease charges, terminal fees, management fees, and interest on shareholder loans. If the non-resident recipient cannot demonstrate actual service provision, functional performance, cost incurrence, and business purpose, the payments are non-deductible. NTS will scrutinise CIM/SMGS billing trails and bill-to-bill markups

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Taxable Income, Net Operating Loss Carryforward, and Loss Limitation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute taxable income after applying statutory net operating loss carryforwards and any loss carryover restrictions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 10-year NOL carryforward period. In cross-border mergers, demergers, or share transfers involving the non-resident ultimate parent, continuity of business and continuity of shareholding must be documented. If the Chusik Hoesa is acquired by a foreign investor and the business continuity requirement is violated, the carried-forward loss may be disallowed

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Progressive Corporate Income Tax Rate Calculation and Local Income Tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate national corporate income tax under the progressive rate schedule and add local income tax surtax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the current Korean brackets: 9% on taxable income up to KRW 200 million; 19% on the excess up to KRW 20 billion; 21% on the excess up to KRW 300 billion; and 24% above KRW 300 billion. Add local income tax surtax of 10% of the national corporate income tax. For a non-resident taxpayer with a Korean PE, tax is computed on Korean-source income attributable to that PE only, and treaty provisions do not exempt the normal Korean tax unless a specific DTA article so provides

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Tax Credits, Foreign Tax Credits, and Incentive Reconciliation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter credits for R&D, job creation, facility investment, foreign taxes paid, and other Restriction of Special Taxation Act incentives
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits are available to the Korean-resident entity for foreign withholding or income taxes paid on profits derived through non-resident operations, subject to per-country limitations. Dividends received from a foreign subsidiary may qualify for an indirect foreign tax credit if the Korean holding percentage and holding period are satisfied. No entity-level credit is available to the non-resident shareholders of the Chusik Hoesa for Korean taxes imposed on the company

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Report of International Transactions and Transfer Pricing Statement
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose all cross-border related-party transactions in rail freight services, railcar leases, intermodal terminal charges, management fees, commission rebates, and intercompany financing
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File the Report of International Transactions with the return where the statutory threshold is triggered. The Korean taxpayer must maintain a Local File and Master File in accordance with OECD transfer pricing documentation standards. The functional analysis must show that Korean personnel perform freight booking, customs interface, rail coordination, container tracking, invoicing, and risk management. A non-resident group company that merely issues an invoice will not be recognised as a legitimate profit driver

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 - Withholding Tax on Outbound Dividend, Interest, and Royalty Payments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report and remit Korean withholding tax on profit distributions, interest, royalties, and other outbound payments to non-resident payees
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Chusik Hoesa declared dividends to a non-resident shareholder during the fiscal year, withhold 22% (20% national corporate income tax plus 2% local income tax surtax) unless a treaty reduction is properly claimed. Attach the Application for Treaty Exemption/Reduction, the non-resident recipient's Tax Residency Certificate, and a Beneficial Ownership Declaration. Interest and royalties paid to non-resident related or unrelated recipients are likewise reported and withheld; a loan principal repayment is not subject to withholding but must be distinguished from disguised dividends

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file the final Corporate Income Tax Return by the statutory deadline triggers additional tax under the Framework Act on National Taxes Article 47-2: 20% of the unpaid tax for a negligent late return and higher rates for intentional non-filing; under-reported or falsely reported taxable income attracts additional tax under Article 47-3 of 10-40% of the understated tax, depending on the degree of fraud; daily overdue interest at approximately 0.022% per day is charged until payment; failure to withhold non-resident tax is assessed against the payer together with a penalty of 10-20% of the un-withheld amount; wilful tax evasion with fraudulent intent subjects the entity and individual directors to criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act with imprisonment up to 5 years, fines up to five times the evaded tax, and Blacklisting / travel-ban measures by the National Tax Service

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% on outbound dividends paid to a non-resident corporate shareholder, comprising 20% national Corporate Income Tax withholding plus 2% local income tax surtax; rate may be reduced to 10-15% under an applicable Bilateral Double Tax Treaty, usually requiring a minimum shareholding and beneficial ownership
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the Korean payer must obtain from the non-resident recipient, before remittance, a signed Application for Non-Resident Corporate Income Tax Exemption/Reduction filed through HomeTax, a current-year Tax Residency Certificate issued by the competent tax authority of the recipient's residence state, a Beneficial Ownership Declaration confirming the recipient is the real economic owner and not a conduit, evidence that the recipient has no permanent establishment in Korea to which the income is effectively connected, and supporting contracts showing the economic nexus of the income. The TRC must be apostilled or consular-certified if required, and translated into Korean. If the application is incomplete, the payer must withhold the full 22% domestic rate; if treaty relief is later denied, NTS assesses the shortfall, interest, and penalties
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory withholding on royalties and interest paid to a non-resident corporation is 22% (20% national plus 2% local). Under typical Korean DTAs, interest may be reduced to 10-15% and royalties to 10-15%, depending on the intellectual property character and beneficial ownership provisions. Korean NTS will examine whether the right is actually used in Korea, whether the royalty amount is arm's length under the transfer pricing rules, and whether the recipient has economic substance. Thin-capitalisation and interest strike-rate limitations may disallow excessive intercompany interest paid to controlling non-resident shareholders

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Under the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs, a Local File is required where the total value of cross-border international related-party transactions exceeds KRW 50 billion in a fiscal year; a Master File is required where the Korean group or local entity meets the consolidated revenue threshold of KRW 100 billion; Country-by-Country reporting applies where the group consolidated revenue of the ultimate parent reaches KRW 100 billion. Even below these thresholds, NTS may request transfer pricing documentation where high-risk transactions are identified
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea does not apply a standalone offshore Economic Substance Regulations regime, but the substance-over-form doctrine under the Framework Act on National Taxes and general anti-avoidance rules require the Chusik Hoesa to have real business activity in Korea. For tax holidays and DTA benefits, the entity must demonstrate actual core income-generating activities in Korea, including rail freight contracting, dispatch, customs clearance, invoicing, operational decision-making, and physical/logistical oversight. A shell Korean company whose profits are in substance controlled from abroad may be recharacterised, denied treaty benefits, subjected to controlled foreign company attribution, or treated as a transparent conduit

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Corporate Income Tax Filing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Chusik Hoesa intentionally underreports transcontinental rail freight revenue, fabricates intercompany logistics expenses, uses fake tax invoices for rail haulage or terminal services, or files a Corporate Income Tax Return containing material false statements with intent to reduce Korean corporate tax and local income tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Article 3, a person who evades tax by fraud or wrongful act is punishable by imprisonment with labor for up to 5 years or a fine not exceeding five times the evaded tax; the corporation is also subject to a joint penal fine under Article 17. Additional taxes of up to 40% of the understated tax, daily overdue interest, and criminal seizure and forfeiture are imposed
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who knowingly signed, directed, or facilitated the fraudulent return is personally exposed to criminal imprisonment and criminal fines. The National Tax Service may issue a departure restriction (travel Blacklisting), attach the director's personal bank accounts and real estate, and invoke secondary tax collection against the director's assets where corporate assets have been dissipated. Civil creditors may claim damages from the director jointly and severally under Commercial Act Article 401, and the corporate veil may be pierced where the Chusik Hoesa is operated as an instrument of tax evasion

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance and Artificial Profit Shifting in Cross-Border Rail Freight
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The corporation charges or pays a non-arm's-length mark-up to a foreign related logistics company, fails to prepare and maintain the Local File and Master File after exceeding the statutory threshold, omits the Report of International Transactions, or shifts Korean operating profit through intercompany railcar leases, rebilling of terminal costs, management fees, or commission structures with a non-resident affiliate that performs no real function
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs, NTS may adjust the transfer price to an arm's-length price by applying the most appropriate method and re-compute taxable income. The adjustment triggers additional corporate income tax of up to 40% under the understatement penalty regime, daily interest, and separate penalties for failure to file international transaction reports; fraudulent documentation may lead to criminal prosecution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve or execute non-arm's-length intercompany agreements without adequate functional and economic analysis are jointly and severally liable to the company and third parties for resulting damages. If the corporate form is used to conceal the real foreign beneficiary, the court may disregard the separate legal personality and permit collection from directors. A director who knowingly signs false transfer pricing documentation faces criminal liability and can be blacklisted from international travel

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Evasion on Profit Repatriation and Abusive Treaty Shopping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Chusik Hoesa pays dividends, interest, or royalties to a non-resident shareholder or affiliate without withholding the 22% statutory amount, or obtains a reduced DTA withholding rate using a Tax Residency Certificate issued to a conduit company that has no beneficial ownership or economic substance, or structures a distribution as a sham loan repayment, service fee, or management charge to avoid Korean dividend withholding
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Korean payer, as statutory withholding agent, is held liable for the un-withheld tax under the Corporate Income Tax Act and must remit the shortfall together with a penalty of 10-20% of the un-withheld amount and daily overdue interest. If treaty benefits are denied, the non-resident recipient becomes subject to Korean tax collection, and deliberate treaty abuse triggers criminal liability under domestic anti-avoidance provisions and general tax fraud sanctions, including imprisonment up to 5 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who resolve to declare dividends, sign sham loan agreements, or approve abusive treaty relief claims are jointly liable for the unpaid withholding tax, additional taxes, and interest. The National Tax Service may pierce the corporate veil to collect from the directors' personal assets where the company is insolvent, and directors may face criminal imprisonment and fines for wilful evasion. Departure restrictions (blacklisting) may be imposed pending full payment of the assessed tax and penalties
